objective: Documenting a risk management plan: roles/responsibilities (RACI), a risk breakdown structure (RBS), and a risk communication plan
secondaryObjectives: Establishing a risk management strategy: processes, templates, metrics, and risk categories
Confirming risk thresholds against organizational risk appetite, and leading stakeholder conflict resolution when appetites disagree

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the risk manager for a fictional regional railway's signalling upgrade: two years, 60 million dollars, work on a live railway. The project has no risk management plan yet.
handover: The sponsor (finance) wants a low cost threshold; the operations director cares most about safety and service.
Contractors keep their own risk lists.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

effects.finding: Finance: escalate any cost risk over 500 thousand dollars. Operations: zero tolerance for safety risk, low tolerance for service disruption.

then.log: Week 2: a contractor rates a signal-interlock risk 'medium' on its own scale and never escalates it; operations finds out from an inspection.
Week 3: the project risk report adds scores from three scales; a high contractor risk appears low overall.
Week 4: a possession overrun risk has no owner; nobody acts on its trigger and trains are delayed the next morning.

else.log: The risk management plan is approved.

thrPrompt.title: Two appetites
thrPrompt.context: Finance and operations disagree on what matters.

choices.label: Facilitate agreed thresholds per objective: any safety risk escalates at once, service disruption over 4 hours escalates, cost over 500 thousand dollars escalates
choices.feedback: Thresholds translate appetite per objective; facilitating resolves the conflict.

choices.label: Use the sponsor's cost threshold for everything
choices.feedback: Safety and service risks below the cost line are never escalated.

choices.label: Define one risk breakdown structure (technical, safety, operational, commercial, external) and one probability-impact scheme every contractor uses

effects.log: One RBS and scale for everyone.

choices.feedback: A common RBS and scale let risks be combined, compared and traced to sources.

choices.label: Map the three scales to each other each month
Keep the three scales
choices.feedback: Risks can't be compared or rolled up.

choices.label: A RACI for identification, analysis, response and monitoring with named risk owners, and a communication plan: weekly contractor reviews, monthly steering report, immediate escalation per threshold
choices.feedback: A plan names who identifies, analyzes, owns and reports, and how risk information flows.

choices.label: The project manager owns every risk
choices.feedback: One person can't own every response on a live railway.

choices.label: Skip roles: everyone is responsible for risk
choices.feedback: Shared by all means owned by none.

reflection.question: Write the summary of the risk management plan for the sponsor.

parts.label: Thresholds and RBS
parts.criteria: Thresholds per objective (safety, service, cost); one RBS and scale.
parts.modelAnswer: Any safety risk escalates at once, service over 4 hours and cost over 500 thousand dollars escalate; everyone uses one RBS and one scale.

parts.label: Roles and communication
parts.criteria: RACI with named owners; weekly, monthly and threshold-triggered communication.
parts.modelAnswer: A RACI names risk owners; contractors review weekly, the steering committee gets a monthly report, and threshold breaches escalate immediately.

scoring.modelReasoning: A risk management plan turns appetite into thresholds per objective (agreed by facilitating conflicting stakeholders), sets one strategy, RBS and scoring scheme so risks can be compared, and documents roles (RACI with named owners) and how risk information is communicated and escalated.
